answers.answer: To turn it on: open Media share in the sidebar, choose Settings, turn on Accept media from viewers, change any other setting or keep the defaults, then choose Save settings. To control the queue: use Approve or Reject on items in Waiting for approval. In Up next, use Play now, Skip and Remove, plus Move up and Move down under More actions. Use Replay, Play now or Remove on played or skipped items in History. Run playback with Play, Pause, Skip to the next item and Stop playback in the On stream card.
answers.quote: Open Media share in the sidebar and choose Settings.

answers.answer: You need the Media share browser source added in OBS from Required overlays on the OBS page before opening submissions. This is stated in the second paragraph. You also need the right permissions: See shared media, Approve or skip shared media, Change the media share settings, and Create and change pipelines for the player, Play now and Replay. All four default to Moderator, as the Who can use this page section states.
answers.quote: Add it from Required overlays on the OBS page, using the browser-source setup, before opening submissions.

answers.answer: A test submission from a viewer below moderator appears under Waiting for approval. After Approve it moves into Up next and plays in OBS, either automatically or with Play in On stream. The On stream card shows the title, the viewer, Playing or Paused, and the time in the item. A moderator's own !media submission skips review, so it does not prove the review step.
answers.quote: Their submission appears under Waiting for approval.

answers.answer: Keep Approve each item before it plays on, which is the default. Ordinary viewer submissions, the passive clip scan and the Submit media step then wait in Waiting for approval. Moderator-or-higher !media submissions and !play still bypass review. To get rid of an unwanted item that is still waiting, choose Reject. If it is already in Up next, choose Remove, then Remove again in the Remove this item? dialog. Either way the item goes to History as rejected, and the bot attempts a refund if the viewer paid.
answers.quote: Choose Remove in the dialog: the item moves to History as rejected, with a refund attempted if the viewer paid.

answers.answer: I reread the Up next row of the queue table to find where Remove sits. The table puts only Move up and Move down inside More actions, and the Skip or remove section does not say where the Remove button is. It costs one glance at the row, not a blocked step.
answers.quote: Choose Remove to take an item out of the queue.

answers.answer: Read aloud, this sentence repeats what the Up next row of the queue table already says, so a listener may wonder whether the first item is a special case. It costs a moment of doubt and nothing more.
answers.quote: Play now is also available on the first item in Up next.

The sentence gives the empty-state message and the permission the player needs, which matters for a moderator about to press Play. The permission already appears in the access table, so the sentence adds no new requirement and costs one line to read.
